subject: Loadproof runbook: ramp schedule, traffic matrix, and artifact handoff
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@impulsepay.com>; SaaS Ops <ops@impulsepay.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-10-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Loadproof runbook: ramp schedule, traffic matrix, and artifact handoff

Alex / team —

Thanks for confirming the go-ahead for the onboarding benchmark window next week. I put together a compact runbook so we have one place for schedule, traffic profiles, acceptance criteria, and where to drop artifacts. High-level: we want to validate sustained throughput and tail latency on your production-like payloads, and produce a single artifacts bundle (CSV + raw traces) that your SREs and our performance engineering team can sign off on.

Key acceptance targets (proposed):
- Sustained throughput: 600 rps for 30m (customer-facing mix)
- 95th percentile latency: < 300 ms
- 99th percentile latency: < 650 ms
- Error rate: < 0.5% (5xx / client timeouts)
- Warmup: prefix cache primed with 1 hour of golden traffic or synthetic warmup described below

Planned ramp schedule (UTC-7):
- 10:00 — baseline validation (50 rps, 10m)
- 10:15 — linear ramp to 300 rps over 10m
- 10:35 — hold 300 rps for 10m (verify stability)
- 10:45 — step to 600 rps over 5m, hold 30m
- 11:20 — cool-down and trace collection (15m)

Traffic matrix and golden payloads are attached (impulsepay-load-matrix.csv). Please confirm the following before we schedule:
1) API keys/endpoint to use (we prefer the staging endpoint that mirrors prod behavior)
2) Any IP allowlist changes needed for our load generator (we’ll provide CIDR)
3) A primary and backup point of contact during the window

Artifact handoff: after the run we will upload the results bundle to the Drive link below and post a short CSV with throughput/latency buckets plus p95/p99. We’ll also provide raw traces (trace IDs) for your team.

I’ve copied Monica (CS lead) and Ben (perf engineer) — can you confirm availability on Oct 5th 10:00 PT? If that works I’ll lock the run and send calendar invites with precise access steps.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Customer Success – Onboarding
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-runbook-20281003.pdf, impulsepay-load-matrix.csv

From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@impulsepay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Lee <jordan@impulsepay.com>
Date: 2028-10-03T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Loadproof runbook: ramp schedule, traffic matrix, and artifact handoff

Thanks Marissa — Oct 5th 10:00 PT works for us. A few items from our side:

- We’ll provide a staging endpoint that mirrors tokenization and payload size. I’ll send creds to the ops address (ops@impulsepay.com) in a separate, encrypted message.
- IP allowlist: add 35.199.120.0/24 and 34.85.200.0/24 (two generator sites)
- Primary contact: me (Alex) during the run; backup: Jordan Lee (SRE)

One ask: we run a short chaos toggle during long holds (brief error injections to validate graceful fallbacks). Can you accommodate a 3-minute controlled error toggle during the 600 rps hold? We want to observe fallback routing and failover metrics.

Also, can you confirm whether the runbook will include the exact key names for metrics we can scrape (e.g., redwood.request.latency.p95)? We’ll wire those into our dashboard.

Appreciate the clear runbook.

—Alex

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>; Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@impulsepay.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-10-03T13:26:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Loadproof runbook: ramp schedule, traffic matrix, and artifact handoff

Alex — we can handle the 3-minute controlled error injection. A couple of clarifications from the perf bench side:

1) Golden payload set: we’ll use the payloads marked as "golden" in impulsepay-load-matrix.csv (IDs 1-30). Those are pre-sanitized to avoid PHI.
2) Metric names: we’ll publish the following to the Drive and expose them via the scrape endpoint you can hook into:
   - redwood.inference.latency.p50
   - redwood.inference.latency.p95
   - redwood.inference.latency.p99
   - redwood.inference.errors.total
   - redwood.inference.throughput.rps
3) Artifact formats: CSV summary (per-minute buckets), traces.json (sampled traces), and results-raw-20281005.json (full event log).

Operational notes: please allow SSH bastion access for one of our engineers (temporary key) so we can collect kernel-level metrics if needed. We’ll only use it for live troubleshooting and will remove the key afterwards.

Ben
Perf Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachment: results-collection-checklist.txt

From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@impulsepay.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>; Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Lee <jordan@impulsepay.com>
Date: 2028-10-04T08:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Loadproof runbook: ramp schedule, traffic matrix, and artifact handoff

Ben — good list. We can:
- Grant temporary bastion access: Jordan will provision a key that expires after 24 hours.
- We’ll wire the metric names into our Grafana dashboard under dashboard ID HS-12345.
- Chaos toggle: Ok for the 3-minute window (we’ll coordinate the exact minute at start-of-hold).

I’ll confirm creds and post the staging endpoint URL by EOD today.

Alex

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>; Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@impulsepay.com>, Jordan Lee <jordan@impulsepay.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-10-05T16:04:00-07:00
Subject: Run complete — initial results uploaded and next steps

Thanks everyone — we executed the run at 10:00 PT and uploaded the artifacts to the Drive link: https://drive.redwood.company/ImpulsePay/Runbook-2028-10-03

Quick summary (first-pass):
- Sustained throughput: 620 rps average during hold (meets target)
- redwood.inference.latency.p95: 285 ms (meets target)
- redwood.inference.latency.p99: 620 ms (meets target)
- Error rate during normal traffic: 0.22% (well under threshold). During the 3-minute chaos toggle we saw errors spike to 3.8% but automatic fallback reduced user-facing errors to 0.9% within 90s.

Artifacts uploaded: results-raw-20281005.json, results-summary-20281005.csv, sampled-traces-20281005.json.

Next steps:
1) Alex / ImpulsePay to review the traces and confirm any SLO tuning they want us to adopt by Oct 12.
2) Redwood to produce a short RCA for the fallback spike and recommended mitigations (expected by Oct 8).
3) If both sides sign the artifacts, we transition the onboarding to the Dedicated deployment plan and schedule a cost estimate session.

Closing note: great collaboration — the run produced clean artifacts and clear signal. I’ll open a follow-up ticket (HS-12345) with the summary and assign action items.

Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: results-raw-20281005.json, results-summary-20281005.csv, sampled-traces-20281005.json
